setup: Set the bar in the rack at mid-thigh height
Overhand grip just outside your thighs
Stand tall, bar hanging on straight arms
Feet about hip to shoulder width
execution: Lift your shoulders straight up to your ears
Keep your arms long; no elbow bend
Hold the top for a moment
Lower slowly to a full stretch
faults: Don't roll your shoulders in circles
Don't bend your elbows to curl the bar
Don't bounce or jerk the weight up

notes: Take the bar from a rack set at mid-thigh height and put it back there, rather than lifting a heavy bar from the floor.
For heavy sets, set the rack's safety arms just below where the bar hangs so you can set it down if your grip fails.
Lifting straps can help when grip gives out before the shoulders do.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Dumbbell shrug
regressions.reason: Lighter loads and the hands can sit at your sides, so the bar can't brush your thighs.

progressions.name: Paused barbell shrug
progressions.reason: A longer hold at the top makes a lighter load harder without more weight.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell shrug
substitutions.reason: Same movement; load is each dumbbell.

substitutions.name: Trap-bar shrug
substitutions.reason: Same movement with the hands at your sides; the trap bar's own weight differs from an Olympic bar.

substitutions.name: Machine shrug
substitutions.reason: Guided path and stack or plate loading; no bar to balance.

substitutions.name: Farmer's carry
substitutions.reason: Heavy loads held at the sides also work the traps and grip.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at shoulder height so the shoulder's straight up-and-down path is clear. Bar seen end-on in front of the thighs. Rack optional in the background.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall, knees soft, arms straight, bar hanging against the front of the thighs. Shoulders relaxed down; neck in line with the spine.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Shoulders lifted straight up toward the ears, arms still straight, bar a few centimetres higher on the thighs. Head stays level and back; no forward poke.

guideBrief.barPath: Short and vertical, close to the thighs
emphasise: The shoulders, not the arms, raise the bar
Straight up and down, no rolling

uncertain.note: Approximate drawing targets, not measured data.
Sources differ slightly on grip width (just outside the thighs vs slightly wider than shoulders). Both are common; the entry uses the narrower, more usual one.
